244	Open items to resolve before encoding anything beyond the table: (1) a measured torque-vs-hours curve for one named calibre would replace the 15 %/day rule; (2) the split between k_e and k_p is an inference from the patent plus bench reports, not a measurement, so the puzzle text should say "most flat-spring watches gain a little as they run down; the escapement alone would make them lose" rather than assert a universal law; (3) Minnix 1968 should be re-fetched when DTIC is back, since it reportedly plots beat-rate error against amplitude² for a real lever escapement.
245	# 04 Positional error: positions, pivot friction, poise
246	
247	Researched 2026-11-01 for the Watchmaker's Bench sim. Scope: (a) the standard positions and why horizontal and vertical differ, (b) poise error and the "220° rule", (c) magnitudes, (d) a formula the sim can use.
248	
249	Confidence labels: **[P]** verified from a primary source (standard, manufacturer document, patent citing the horological literature); **[S]** plausible, secondary only (blogs, forum practitioners); **[U]** could not verify.
250	
251	## (a) Positions and why horizontal differs from vertical
252	
253	**Vocabulary [P].** Witschi's *Testing of mechanical watches* (2025 PDF, p. 21) lists the six industry positions: dial up (CH), dial down (CB), crown down (9H), crown left (6H), crown up (3H), crown right (12H). The `nH` code names the hour index that sits at the **top**: the Rolex patent US10120341B2 defines 12H as "the index 12H of the dial ... situated at the top relative to the vector g" and 3H as "with the movement shaft at the top", citing NIHS notation and *Traité de construction horlogère* p. 741. ISO 3159 / COSC use five of these: 6H, 3H, 9H, FH (fond haut = dial down, Witschi's CB) and CH; 12H (crown right) is not tested (COSC: "tested in 5 positions"; Wikipedia lists "3 o'clock, 6 o'clock, 9 o'clock, dial on top, dial on the bottom"). Note Witschi's own p. 27 calls 6H "crown down", contradicting its p. 21 and the patent; treat 6H = crown left, 9H = crown down.
254	
255	**Why vertical is worse [P for mechanism, S for the numbers].** Witschi p. 21 gives three reasons for multi-position testing: gravity acting on balance and escapement, imbalance of the balance, and "friction in the balance bearings varies with the position of the watch, leading to changes in both amplitude and rate". SJX (Richard Lee and Ashton Tracy, 2020) describe the geometry: dial up/down "has the least friction, with the main contact being the tip of the lower pivot ... akin to a spinning top on a table", while on its side "both pivots [are] turning against the wall of the bearings ... akin to a pen being laid flat", so "friction on the pivots will always be higher when the watch is placed on its side" and the visible symptom is "a drop in amplitude".
256	
257	**Size of the amplitude drop.** Witschi's worked six-position dataset (p. 26) is a real-looking example: fully wound CH 298°, CB 294°, vertical 278–287°; after 24 h horizontal 286–298°, vertical 264–279°. Its DVH amplitude value is −12° at 0 h **[P, one example]**. Practitioner consensus on watchrepairtalk is "around 30° (±10°)" for wristwatches, ~40° for slow-beat vintage, ~60° for Unitas 6498 pocket calibres; drops near 100° indicate a fault (pivot ends polished too round, excess lock) **[S]**. Witschi p. 12: healthy full-wind amplitude 270–310°, lift angle ≈ 51° for most modern movements **[P]**.
258	
259	## (b) Poise error and the 220° rule
260	
261	**What it is [P].** The Rolex patent defines static imbalance as "the product of the mass of the balance times the distance between its center of gravity and the axis of rotation ... typically measured in µg·cm or nN·m. With terrestrial gravity, 1 µg·cm corresponds to approximately 0.1 nN·m." It states, citing J.-J. Augsburger, *La mise d'équilibre des balanciers*, Proc. Swiss Chronometry Congress 1966 p. 324: the rate effect "is proportional to the imbalance itself", "inversely proportional to the inertia of the balance", "highly dependent on the amplitude of oscillation ... It is even cancelled out completely for an amplitude close to 220°", "varies as the sine of the azimuth angle between the axis of the balance ... and the vertical" (so zero when dial up/down) and "varies with the angle between the direction of the imbalance and the vertical", with two opposite vertical positions where it vanishes and two, 90° away, where it is maximal. A second zero exists near 400° (patent, description).
262	
263	**Why 220° [P, derivation checked here].** Put the heavy spot at angle φ from the downward vertical when the balance is at rest (φ = 0: heavy spot at the bottom). Gravity adds the torque −g·u·cos φ·sin θ to the hairspring's −k·θ (u = mass × eccentricity; the sin φ part only shifts the rest position and is second order). Harmonic balance of sin(Θ cos ωt) gives a fundamental 2J1(Θ)cos ωt, so
264	
265	    ω² = ω0² · [1 + (g·u·cos φ / (I·ω0²)) · 2·J1(Θ)/Θ]
266	    rate [s/d] ≈ 86400 · (g · u · cos φ / (I · ω0²)) · J1(Θ)/Θ
267	
268	with I the balance inertia, ω0 = 2πf, Θ the amplitude in radians (zero to turning point, the timegrapher convention). J1's first zero is 3.8317 rad = **219.54°**, which is the 220° rule. The patent's claim 9 is exactly the least-squares inverse of this expression: `3H(θ) − 9H(θ) = 2·86400·g·bx /(I·(2πf)²) · J1(θ)/θ`, with x the 9H direction, so the model and the primary source agree on form and on the (2πf)² factor.
269	
270	**Sign [P via patent axes, S via practitioners].** In the patent, bx > 0 (heavy spot toward the 9H index) makes 3H(θ) − 9H(θ) positive for Θ < 220°; in position 3H the 9H index is at the bottom. Hence: **heavy spot at the bottom at rest, amplitude below 220° → the watch gains; above 220° → it loses; heavy spot at the top is the mirror image.** Practitioners state the same: "influence is zero at about 220 degrees, and it changes from fast to slow under and over 220 deg", and the Greiner dynamic-poising procedure (Mark, watchrepairtalk, 19 Dec 2014) tests at 150–180° and takes the fastest vertical position as the one with the heavy spot down. Physical picture (forum, [S]): at low amplitude the heavy spot stays near the bottom and gravity stiffens the restoring torque like a pendulum; above 220° it spends enough of each swing past the horizontal that the net effect reverses.
271	
272	**Dynamic poising at one amplitude is unreliable [P].** The patent, quoting Vermot et al. *Traité de construction horlogère* (PPUR 2011, pp. 190–200), warns that single-amplitude "rate to positions" poising "lacks precision" because other position errors (hairspring, escapement) are mixed in; Rolex's method fits the J1 curve across amplitudes either side of 220°. A side note: WO2012007460 recommends correcting at 137° or 316.5° (the zeros of J0) so the material removed does not itself unbalance; that is a manufacturing detail, not a rate rule **[U, not pursued]**.
273

279	| mean variation in rates | ≤ 2 s/d | Wikipedia table from von Osterhausen [S] |
280	| greatest variation in rates (one position, day to day) | ≤ 5 s/d | same [S] |
281	| difference horizontal − vertical (mean CH/FH days 9–10 minus mean 6H days 1–2) | −6 / +8 s/d | same [S] |
282	| largest variation in rates (any rate vs mean) | ≤ 10 s/d | same [S] |
283	| thermal variation | ±0.6 s/d/°C; rate resumption ±5 s/d | same [S] |
284	| Test: 15 days, 5 positions, 8 / 23 / 38 °C | | COSC FAQ [P] |
285	| Witschi worked example: max position delta D | 8.0 s/d at 0 h, 9.1 s/d at 24 h; DVH −2.1 s/d | Witschi p. 26–27 [P, example] |
286	| Patent example: position spread before/after balancing | ≈ ±7 s/d → ±2–3 s/d; apparent imbalance 10.5 → <0.2 µg·cm | US10120341B2 [P] |
287	| Good milled balance alone | mean residual 1.5 µg·cm | Augsburger 1966 via patent [P] |
288	| Correction range of Rolex inertia blocks | ≥ 20 µg·cm | patent [P] |
289	| Balance inertia, 4 Hz wristwatch | ≈ 12 mg·cm² (patent design example, ≥ 12·10⁻¹⁰ kg·m²; engineering calculator 1.2·10⁻⁹ kg·m²) | [S] |
290	| Practitioner tolerance for vertical spread after poising | within ±60 s/d is "properly poised" (forum) | [S] |
291	
292	Model check (computed from the formula above, f = 4 Hz, I = 12 mg·cm², cos φ = 1): 10 µg·cm gives about +37 s/d at 100°, +20 at 150°, +10 at 180°, 0 at 219.5°, −3.6 at 240°, −6.7 at 270°, −7.4 at 300°. A 10 µg·cm fault at full wind therefore reads as a 10–15 s/d spread between opposite vertical positions, which matches the patent's "±7 s/d" example in scale.
293	
294	## Could not verify
295	
296	- Daniels *Watchmaking*, de Carle, Jendritzki and Fried were not reachable online; no quote from them is used. Ciechanowski's *Mechanical Watch* covers regulator and beat adjustment but says nothing about positions or poise.
297	- ISO 3159's day-by-day position schedule (6H days 1–2 ... CH days 9–10) is inferred from the Wikipedia footnote on criterion D, not from the standard text.
298	- Whether the vertical amplitude drop should be modelled as viscous or Coulomb friction is not settled by any source found; the brief's 20–60° range is consistent with everything above but no primary source states a range.
299

304	| Positions | Six: CH (dial up), CB/FH (dial down), 9H crown down, 6H crown left, 3H crown up, 12H crown right. Puzzles and the COSC check use the ISO five (drop 12H). | High [P] |

Use a series or `besselj` for J1. | High [P] |
307	| Sign convention | Heavy spot at bottom (φ = 0), Θ < 219.5°: gains. Θ > 219.5°: loses. Crossover 219.54° (first zero of J1); second zero ≈ 400°, irrelevant. | High [P] |

309	| Pass/fail readout | COSC-style: horizontal − vertical within −6/+8 s/d, largest position spread ≤ 10 s/d, mean rate −4/+6 s/d. | High for −4/+6 [P], medium for the rest [S] |

60	    19	/** Separating-axis test for two convex polygons. Returns penetration depth (>0 means overlap). */
61	    20	export function penetration(a: Polygon, b: Polygon): number {
62	    21	  let minOverlap = Infinity;
63	    22	  for (const poly of [a, b]) {
64	    23	    for (let i = 0; i < poly.length; i++) {
65	    24	      const p = poly[i], q = poly[(i + 1) % poly.length];
66	    25	      const axis = v(-(q.y - p.y), q.x - p.x);
67	    26	      const l = len(axis);
68	    27	      if (l === 0) continue;
69	    28	      const n = scale(axis, 1 / l);
70	    29	      const [a0, a1] = project(a, n), [b0, b1] = project(b, n);
71	    30	      const overlap = Math.min(a1, b1) - Math.max(a0, b0);
72	    31	      if (overlap < minOverlap) minOverlap = overlap;
73	    32	    }
74	    33	  }
75	    34	  return minOverlap;
76	    35	}
77	    36	
78	    37	function project(poly: Polygon, n: Vec): [number, number] {
79	    38	  let lo = Infinity, hi = -Infinity;
80	    39	  for (const p of poly) { const d = dot(p, n); if (d < lo) lo = d; if (d > hi) hi = d; }
81	    40	  return [lo, hi];
82	    41	}

84	    43	/** Distance from a point to a segment. */
85	    44	export function distToSegment(p: Vec, a: Vec, b: Vec): number {
86	    45	  const ab = sub(b, a), ap = sub(p, a);
87	    46	  const t = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, dot(ap, ab) / Math.max(dot(ab, ab), 1e-12)));
88	    47	  return len(sub(p, add(a, scale(ab, t))));
89	    48	}

105	    15	export interface EscapementPose {

111	    21	  /** Count of steps where lever motion drove a stone into a tooth by more than NUDGE_TOL degrees. */

125	    35	 *  whenever the pin is out of the notch (zero draw: nothing else moves it). */
126	    36	export function forkFor(p: EscapementParams, balanceAngle: number): number {

129	    39	  return (x / half) * derived(p).forkHalf;
130	    40	}

132	    42	/** A pose with the wheel settled against whichever stone the given balance angle locks. */
133	    43	export function initialPose(p: EscapementParams, balanceAngle: number): EscapementPose {

146	    56	 *  `driven` is whether the gear train still delivers torque to the escape wheel: a run-down watch
147	    57	 *  has none, so its wheel moves only if a pallet stone pushes it. */

158	    68	function substep(p: EscapementParams, prev: EscapementPose, bal: number, dt: number, driven: boolean): EscapementPose {

183	    93	  return { balanceAngle: bal, forkAngle: fork, wheelAngle: wheel, phase, contact, violations, maxNudge };

186	    96	/** Largest penetration between any tooth and either stone. */
187	    97	function worst(p: EscapementParams, forkAngle: number, wheelAngle: number) {
188	    98	  const { entryStone, exitStone } = stones(p, forkAngle);
189	    99	  let max = -Infinity;
190	   100	  for (const tooth of toothPolygons(p, wheelAngle)) {
191	   101	    for (const s of [entryStone, exitStone]) {
192	   102	      const pen = stonePenetration(tooth, s);
193	   103	      if (pen > max) max = pen;
194	   104	    }
195	   105	  }
196	   106	  return max;
197	   107	}

199	   109	function classify(p: EscapementParams, forkAngle: number, wheelAngle: number): { stone: StoneName; face: Face } {
200	   110	  const { entryStone, exitStone } = stones(p, forkAngle);
201	   111	  let best = { d: Infinity, stone: "entry" as StoneName, face: "locking" as Face };
202	   112	  for (const tooth of toothPolygons(p, wheelAngle)) {
203	   113	    const tip = tooth[0];
204	   114	    for (const [name, s] of [["entry", entryStone], ["exit", exitStone]] as const) {
205	   115	      const dImp = distToSegment(tip, s.corner, s.letoff);
206	   116	      const dLock = Math.abs(len(sub(tip, s.pivot)) - s.lockRadius);
207	   117	      if (dImp < best.d) best = { d: dImp, stone: name, face: "impulse" };
208	   118	      if (dLock < best.d) best = { d: dLock, stone: name, face: "locking" };
209	   119	    }
210	   120	  }
211	   121	  return { stone: best.stone, face: best.face };
212	   122	}

214	   124	/** Nearest wheel angle (either direction, within half a degree) at which the pose no longer penetrates. */
215	   125	function clear(p: EscapementParams, fork: number, wheel: number) {

222	   132	    }
223	   133	    return hi;
224	   134	  };

226	   136	  if (fwd === Infinity && back === Infinity) return wheel + 0.5; // hopeless; let the violation show

230	   140	/** Move the wheel forward by up to `maxStep` degrees, stopping at first contact. */
231	   141	function advance(p: EscapementParams, fork: number, wheel: number, maxStep: number) {

236	   146	    const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
237	   147	    if (worst(p, fork, mid) <= CONTACT_TOL) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
238	   148	  }
239	   149	  return { wheel: lo, blocked: true };
240	   150	}

242	     1	/**
243	     2	 * Pure geometry: parameters + state in, shapes out. The renderer draws these; the
244	     3	 * simulation uses the same description for contact, so what you see is what is computed.

249	     8	import { type Polygon, type Vec, add, scale, polar, rotateAbout, sub, len, dot, v } from "./geom2d";

251	    10	export interface Pose { balanceAngle: number; forkAngle: number; wheelAngle: number }
252	    11	// (Pose is the subset of EscapementPose the drawing needs.)
253	    12	
254	    13	/**
255	    14	 * A pallet stone, exactly: an annular sector about the fork pivot, cut by the impulse
256	    15	 * plane. The locking face is the arc at radius `lockRadius`, so lever rotation slides it
257	    16	 * along itself (zero draw). Angles are radians about the pivot, measured with atan2.
258	    17	 */
259	    18	export interface Stone {
260	    19	  pivot: Vec;
261	    20	  lockRadius: number;
262	    21	  /** Radial band about the pivot that holds the stone body; one bound is the lock arc. */
263	    22	  rLo: number;
264	    23	  rHi: number;
265	    24	  /** Impulse plane: inside the stone when dot(q - corner, normal) >= 0. */
266	    25	  corner: Vec;
267	    26	  normal: Vec;
268	    27	  /** Back edge, from the let-off corner away from the wheel: inside when dot(q - letoff, backNormal) >= 0. */
269	    28	  letoff: Vec;
270	    29	  backNormal: Vec;
271	    30	  /** Top edge, closing the slab: inside when dot(q - outerEnd, topNormal) >= 0. */
272	    31	  outerEnd: Vec;
273	    32	  backEnd: Vec;
274	    33	  topNormal: Vec;
275	    34	  /** Whether the stone body lies at radii below (`inside`) or above the lock arc. */
276	    35	  bodyInside: boolean;
277	    36	}

279	    38	/** Signed depth of a point inside a stone: positive inside, negative outside. */
280	    39	export function stoneDepth(q: Vec, s: Stone): number {
281	    40	  const r = len(sub(q, s.pivot));
282	    41	  return Math.min(
283	    42	    r - s.rLo,
284	    43	    s.rHi - r,
285	    44	    dot(sub(q, s.corner), s.normal),
286	    45	    dot(sub(q, s.letoff), s.backNormal),
287	    46	    dot(sub(q, s.outerEnd), s.topNormal),
288	    47	  );
289	    48	}

291	    50	/** Largest depth of any tooth vertex inside a stone. */
292	    51	export function stonePenetration(tooth: Polygon, stone: Stone): number {
293	    52	  let max = -Infinity;
294	    53	  for (const q of tooth) {
295	    54	    const dd = stoneDepth(q, stone);
296	    55	    if (dd > max) max = dd;
297	    56	  }
298	    57	  return max;
299	    58	}

301	    60	/** Outline for drawing: the lock arc chorded finely, then the three straight edges. */
302	    61	export function stoneOutline(s: Stone, chords = 24): Polygon {
303	    62	  const a0 = Math.atan2(s.corner.y - s.pivot.y, s.corner.x - s.pivot.x);
304	    63	  let a1 = Math.atan2(s.outerEnd.y - s.pivot.y, s.outerEnd.x - s.pivot.x);
305	    64	  while (a1 - a0 > Math.PI) a1 -= 2 * Math.PI;
306	    65	  while (a1 - a0 < -Math.PI) a1 += 2 * Math.PI;
307	    66	  const arc = Array.from({ length: chords + 1 }, (_, i) => add(s.pivot, polar(s.lockRadius, a0 + ((a1 - a0) * i) / chords)));
308	    67	  return [...arc, s.backEnd, s.letoff];
309	    68	}

311	    70	export function fixedPoints(p: EscapementParams) {
312	    71	  const d = derived(p);
313	    72	  const forkPivot = v(0, d.pivotDistance);
314	    73	  const pinOrbit = (p.forkLength * rad(d.forkHalf)) / rad(p.liftAngle / 2);
315	    74	  const balanceCentre = v(0, d.pivotDistance + p.forkLength + pinOrbit);
316	    75	  return { d, forkPivot, balanceCentre, pinOrbit };
317	    76	}

319	    78	/** Stone in the lever frame (fork angle 0), built so the tooth tip rests exactly on the
320	    79	 *  lock arc at the tangent point when the lever is on the banking `lockedAt`. */
321	    80	function stoneAtRest(p: EscapementParams, tangentAngleDeg: number, lockedAt: number): Stone {

361	   120	  if (dot(sub(corner, outerEnd), topNormal) < 0) topNormal = scale(topNormal, -1);
362	   121	
363	   122	  const unrotated: Stone = {
364	   123	    pivot: P,
365	   124	    lockRadius: L,
366	   125	    rLo,
367	   126	    rHi,
368	   127	    corner,
369	   128	    normal,
370	   129	    letoff,
371	   130	    backNormal,
372	   131	    outerEnd,
373	   132	    backEnd,
374	   133	    topNormal,
375	   134	    bodyInside,
376	   135	  };

380	   139	function rotateStone(s: Stone, angleRad: number): Stone {
381	   140	  const r = (q: Vec) => rotateAbout(q, s.pivot, angleRad);
382	   141	  const rv = (q: Vec) => rotateAbout(q, v(0, 0), angleRad);

385	   144	    corner: r(s.corner), letoff: r(s.letoff), outerEnd: r(s.outerEnd), backEnd: r(s.backEnd),
386	   145	    normal: rv(s.normal), backNormal: rv(s.backNormal), topNormal: rv(s.topNormal),
387	   146	  };
388	   147	}

390	   149	const restCache = new WeakMap<EscapementParams, { entry: Stone; exit: Stone }>();
391	   150	export function stonesAtRest(p: EscapementParams) {
392	   151	  let c = restCache.get(p);
393	   152	  if (!c) {
394	   153	    const { d } = fixedPoints(p);
395	   154	    c = {
396	   155	      entry: stoneAtRest(p, 90 + d.halfEmbrace, +d.forkHalf),
397	   156	      exit: stoneAtRest(p, 90 - d.halfEmbrace, -d.forkHalf),
398	   157	    };

400	   159	  }
401	   160	  return c;

404	   163	export function toothPolygons(p: EscapementParams, wheelAngle: number): Polygon[] {
405	   164	  const { d } = fixedPoints(p);
406	   165	  const R = p.wheelRadius;
407	   166	  const out: Polygon[] = [];

411	   170	    out.push([polar(R, tip), polar(0.8 * R, tip + rad(2)), polar(0.8 * R, tip + rad(10))]);
412	   171	  }
413	   172	  return out;
414	   173	}

440	   199	export function shapes(p: EscapementParams, pose: Pose): Shapes {
441	   200	  const { forkPivot, balanceCentre, pinOrbit } = fixedPoints(p);
442	   201	  const { entryStone, exitStone } = stones(p, pose.forkAngle);

449	   208	    add(forkPivot, v(-half, 0)), add(forkPivot, v(half, 0)),
450	   209	    add(forkPivot, v(half, L - 12)), add(forkPivot, v(horn + 2, L - 12)), add(forkPivot, v(horn + 2, L + 6)),
451	   210	    add(forkPivot, v(horn, L + 6)), add(forkPivot, v(horn, L - 6)), add(forkPivot, v(-horn, L - 6)),
452	   211	    add(forkPivot, v(-horn, L + 6)), add(forkPivot, v(-horn - 2, L + 6)), add(forkPivot, v(-horn - 2, L - 12)),
453	   212	    add(forkPivot, v(-half, L - 12)),
454	   213	  ];

457	   216	    const tip = scale(add(st.outerEnd, st.backEnd), 0.5);

     1	/** Timegrapher panel: trace plus readouts. Reads a Reading; computes nothing but pixels. */
     2	import type { Reading } from "../core/timegrapher/analyze";
     3	
     4	export interface TimegrapherView {
     5	  reading: Reading | null;
     6	  nominalPeriod: number;
     7	  liftAngle: number;
     8	  running: boolean;
     9	  knocking: boolean;
    10	  /** Sim seconds the trace spans, for the honest label. */
    11	  spanSeconds: number;
    12	  /** Sim seconds per wall second, for the honest label. */
    13	  speedup: number;
    14	}
    15	
    16	const fmt = (x: number, d: number) => (Math.abs(x) < 0.5 * 10 ** -d ? "" : x > 0 ? "+" : "−") + Math.abs(x).toFixed(d);
    17	
    18	export function renderTimegrapher(v: TimegrapherView): string {
    19	  const W = 420, H = 300, pad = 36;
    20	  const beatMs = (v.nominalPeriod / 2) * 1000;
    21	  const yRange = Math.min(20, beatMs / 2); // ±20 ms, wrapping like a real machine's screen
    22	  const r = v.reading;
    23	  const dots = r
    24	    ? r.trace.map((p) => {
    25	        const x = pad + ((W - 2 * pad) * p.beat) / Math.max(1, r.trace.length - 1);
    26	        let off = ((p.offsetMs + yRange) % (2 * yRange) + 2 * yRange) % (2 * yRange) - yRange; // wrap
    27	        const y = H / 2 - (off / yRange) * (H / 2 - pad);
    28	        return `<circle class="dot p${p.parity}" cx="${x.toFixed(1)}" cy="${y.toFixed(1)}" r="1.5"/>`;
    29	      }).join("")
    30	    : "";
    31	  const rate = r && v.running ? fmt(r.rateSecondsPerDay, 0) : "—";
    32	  const amp = r && v.running ? r.amplitudeDeg.toFixed(0) : "—";
    33	  const be = r && v.running ? r.beatErrorMs.toFixed(1) : "—";
    34	  // Faint horizontal grid at ±10 ms: half the screen range, purely a reading aid.
    35	  const gridY = [H / 2 - (H / 2 - pad) / 2, H / 2 + (H / 2 - pad) / 2];
    36	  return `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 ${W} ${H + 84}" class="timegrapher" data-rate="${r?.rateSecondsPerDay ?? ""}">
    37	  <rect x="0" y="0" width="${W}" height="${H}" rx="2" class="screen"/>
    38	  <rect x="0.5" y="0.5" width="${W - 1}" height="${H - 1}" rx="2" class="screen-edge"/>
    39	  ${gridY.map((y) => `<line x1="${pad}" y1="${y}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${y}" class="grid"/>`).join("")}
    40	  <line x1="${pad}" y1="${H / 2}" x2="${W - pad}" y2="${H / 2}" class="axis"/>
    41	  <text x="${pad}" y="${pad - 10}" class="axislabel">+${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
    42	  <text x="${pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel">−${yRange.toFixed(0)} ms</text>
    43	  <text x="${W - pad}" y="${H - pad + 18}" class="axislabel" text-anchor="end">${v.spanSeconds.toFixed(0)} s of ticks at ${v.speedup}× time</text>
    44	  ${v.knocking ? `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">Knocking: amplitude unreliable</text>` : ""}
    45	  ${v.running ? dots : `<text x="${W / 2}" y="${H / 2}" class="warn" text-anchor="middle">No signal. The watch has stopped.</text>`}
    46	  <g class="readouts" transform="translate(0,${H + 10})">
    47	    <line x1="${W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
    48	    <line x1="${2 * W / 3}" y1="8" x2="${2 * W / 3}" y2="56" class="divider"/>
    49	    <text x="${pad}" y="34" class="big">${rate}<tspan class="unit"> s/day</tspan></text>
    50	    <text x="${W / 2}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="middle">${amp}<tspan class="unit">°</tspan></text>
    51	    <text x="${W - pad}" y="34" class="big" text-anchor="end">${be}<tspan class="unit"> ms</tspan></text>
    52	    <text x="${pad}" y="56" class="small">rate</text>
    53	    <text x="${W / 2}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="middle">amplitude at ${v.liftAngle}° lift angle</text>
    54	    <text x="${W - pad}" y="56" class="small" text-anchor="end">beat error</text>
    55	  </g>
    56	</svg>`;
    57	}
=== src/view/speed.ts
     1	/** Movement speed control: a stepped slider inside the drawing panel.
     2	 *  It drives the hidden <select id="speed"> that main.ts listens to, so the frame loop is untouched. */
     3	
     4	export const SPEED_STOPS: { value: number; label: string }[] = [
     5	  { value: 0.01, label: "1/100" },
     6	  { value: 0.05, label: "1/20" },
     7	  { value: 0.1, label: "1/10" },
     8	  { value: 0.2, label: "1/5" },
     9	  { value: 1, label: "real time" },
    10	];
    11	export const DEFAULT_SPEED = 0.1;
    12	
    13	export function mountSpeedControl(host: HTMLElement, select: HTMLSelectElement, pause: HTMLElement): void {
    14	  const start = Math.max(0, SPEED_STOPS.findIndex((s) => s.value === DEFAULT_SPEED));
    15	  host.innerHTML = `<label class="tempo-label" for="speed-slider">Movement speed</label>
    16	    <div class="tempo-track">
    17	      <input id="speed-slider" type="range" min="0" max="${SPEED_STOPS.length - 1}" step="1" value="${start}" aria-valuetext="${SPEED_STOPS[start].label}" />
    18	      <div class="tempo-stops" aria-hidden="true" style="--n:${SPEED_STOPS.length - 1}">${SPEED_STOPS.map((s, i) => `<span style="--i:${i}">${s.label}</span>`).join("")}</div>
    19	    </div>`;
    20	  host.appendChild(pause);
    21	  const slider = host.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>("#speed-slider")!;
    22	  const apply = () => {
    23	    const stop = SPEED_STOPS[Number(slider.value)];
    24	    slider.setAttribute("aria-valuetext", stop.label);
    25	    host.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(".tempo-stops span").forEach((el, i) => el.classList.toggle("on", i === Number(slider.value)));
    26	    select.value = String(stop.value);
    27	    select.dispatchEvent(new Event("change"));
    28	  };
    29	  slider.oninput = apply;
    30	  apply();
    31	}

    17	function trajectory(periods: number, stepsPerPeriod = 4000) {

    26	    pose = step(p, pose, bal(t), dt);
    27	    out.push({ t, pose });
    28	  }
    29	  return out;

> function trajectory(periods: number, stepsPerPeriod = 4000) {
>   const bal = (t: number) => AMPLITUDE * Math.sin((2 * Math.PI * t) / T);

260	   260	/** The step-by-step guide. Returns open(step, switchToFreePlay) so the strip can replay it. */

263	   263	  backdrop.id = "guide-backdrop"; backdrop.hidden = true;
264	   264	  const frames = document.createElement("div");
265	   265	  frames.id = "guide-frames"; frames.hidden = true;

272	   272	  let step = 0, open = false, selectors: Spot[] = [], raf = 0;
273	   273	  const narrow = () => window.matchMedia("(max-width: 760px)").matches;
274	   274	  /** Phones only: the page is padded below the card, since there is no side to dock it on.

280	   280	    if (need <= band) return;

283	   283	  };
284	   284	  /** The job that was selected when the guide opened; Skip puts it back. */

287	   287	  type Box = { l: number; t: number; r: number; b: number };
288	   288	  /** Padded union of one selector's visible elements, in viewport pixels. */
289	   289	  const measure = (spot: Spot): Box | null => {
290	   290	    const selector = typeof spot === "string" ? spot : spot.sel, PAD = typeof spot === "string" ? 8 : spot.pad;
291	   291	    let l = Infinity, t = Infinity, r = -Infinity, b = -Infinity, n = 0;
292	   292	    for (const el of Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<Element>(selector))) {

331	   331	    const all = boxes();

395	   395	      ${s.fix ? `<div class="fix"><small>${first ? "" : "On the bench"}</small>${s.fix}</div>` : ""}
396	   396	      ${s.manual ? `<p class="manual">Read more in the manual: <a href="${MANUAL}#${s.manual.anchor}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">${s.manual.label} ↗</a> (Ciechanowski, <i>Mechanical Watch</i>)</p>` : ""}
397	   397	      <div class="nav">
398	   398	        <span class="dots">${first ? "" : `${step} of ${STEPS.length - 1}`}</span>
399	   399	        ${first ? `<button type="button" class="skip" data-act="skip">Skip, I know watches</button>` : `<button type="button" class="skip" data-act="skip">Skip</button>`}
400	   400	        ${first ? "" : `<button type="button" data-act="back">Back</button>`}
401	   401	        <button type="button" class="primary" data-act="next">${first ? "Start" : last ? "Start fixing" : "Next"}</button>
402	   402	      </div>`;
403	   403	    card.querySelectorAll<HTMLButtonElement>("[data-act]").forEach((b) => (b.onclick = () => act(b.dataset.act!)));

405	   405	    resetControls();
406	   406	    setSpeed(String(s.speed ?? 0));

408	   408	    spot(s.spot);

410	   410	  };

412	   412	    open = false; cancelAnimationFrame(raf); selectors = [];

458	   458	export function mountOnboarding(): void {
459	   459	  const main = document.querySelector("main");
460	   460	  const puzzleEl = document.getElementById("puzzle");
461	   461	  if (!main || !puzzleEl) return;
462	   462	
463	   463	  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
464	   464	  const forced = FORCED[params.get("state") ?? ""];
465	   465	  // Design's named states must screenshot without this layer; only onboarding's own states show it.
466	   466	  if (params.has("state") && !forced) return;
467	   467	
468	   468	  document.head.appendChild(Object.assign(document.createElement("style"), { textContent: STYLE }));
469	   469	
470	   470	  // The strip between the title block and the two pictures: replay, explainer, hint. Never covers the controls.
471	   471	  const strip = document.createElement("section");
472	   472	  strip.id = "onboarding";
473	   473	  strip.setAttribute("aria-label", "Guide");
474	   474	  strip.innerHTML = STRIP;
475	   475	  main.before(strip);
476	   476	  const details = strip.querySelector("details")!;
477	   477	  const hintEl = strip.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".hint")!;
478	   478	
479	   479	  // Progressive hint: one per puzzle, after 60 wall-seconds without the hold bar moving or an answer chosen.
480	   480	  // The clock restarts when the guide closes, so time spent reading does not count.
481	   481	  const select = document.getElementById("puzzle-select") as HTMLSelectElement | null;
482	   482	  let puzzleId = select?.value ?? "";
483	   483	  let since = performance.now();
484	   484	  const showHint = (id: string) => {
485	   485	    const text = HINTS[id];
486	   486	    if (!text) return;
487	   487	    hintEl.innerHTML = `<span class="tag">Hint</span>${text}`;
488	   488	    hintEl.hidden = false;
489	   489	  };
490	   490	  const progressed = () => {
491	   491	    const bar = puzzleEl.querySelector(".hold span")?.textContent ?? "";
492	   492	    if (bar && !bar.startsWith("0 /")) return true;
493	   493	    if (puzzleEl.querySelector(".choice.right, .choice.wrong")) return true;
494	   494	    return false;
495	   495	  };
496	   496	  let guideOpen = false;
497	   497	  const tick = () => {
498	   498	    const now = select?.value ?? "";
499	   499	    if (now !== puzzleId) { puzzleId = now; since = performance.now(); hintEl.hidden = true; }
500	   500	    if (guideOpen) { since = performance.now(); return; }
501	   501	    if (!hintEl.hidden || !puzzleId) return;
502	   502	    if (progressed()) { since = performance.now(); return; }
503	   503	    if (performance.now() - since >= HINT_AFTER_MS) showHint(puzzleId);
504	   504	  };
505	   505	
506	   506	  const openGuide = mountGuide(() => { guideOpen = false; since = performance.now(); });
507	   507	  const startGuide = (at = 0, freePlay = true) => { guideOpen = true; openGuide(at, freePlay); };
508	   508	  strip.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('[data-act="replay"]')!.onclick = () => startGuide(0);
509	   509	
510	   510	  if (forced?.kind === "guide") { startGuide(forced.step, false); return; }
511	   511	  if (forced?.kind === "trace") { details.open = true; return; }
512	   512	  if (forced?.kind === "hint") { showHint(puzzleId); return; }
513	   513	
514	   514	  // Scripted browsers (the solve and drag scripts) load "/" and expect puzzle 1, so the guide opens
515	   515	  // for them only when the URL asks with ?guide.
516	   516	  const scripted = navigator.webdriver && !params.has("guide");
517	   517	  if (read(GUIDE_DONE_KEY) !== "1" && !scripted) startGuide(0);
518	   518	  setInterval(tick, 1000);
519	   519	}

     2	# Deploy a branch of the Watchmaker's Bench to Cloudflare Pages.
     3	#
     4	#   deploy.sh <branch> [--as <remote-name>] [--promote]
     5	#
     6	# Preview (default): verify the branch tip in a throwaway worktree (npm ci, npm test,
     7	# npm run build), push it to origin, wait for the Cloudflare build, confirm the preview
     8	# URL serves that build.
     9	# --promote: after the preview, fast-forward main to the same tip and confirm production.
    10	#            Only with Akash's go-ahead; see SKILL.md.
    11	# --as:      remote branch name when it differs from the local one (worktree-foo -> foo).
    12	#
    13	# Never force-pushes, never deletes remote branches, never touches any checkout's
    14	# working tree. Exit 0 on success, non-zero with a reason otherwise.
    15	set -euo pipefail
    16	
    17	GH_REPO=ahparikh/watchmakers-bench
    18	PROJECT=watchmakers-bench
    19	PROD_URL="https://${PROJECT}.pages.dev"
    20	BUILD_TIMEOUT=300   # seconds to wait for a Cloudflare build
    21	SERVE_TIMEOUT=120   # seconds to wait for the URL to serve the new bundle

    28	    --promote) PROMOTE=1; shift;;
    29	    *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 64;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	[ -n "$BRANCH" ] || { echo "usage: deploy.sh <branch> [--as <remote-name>] [--promote]" >&2; exit 64; }
    33	AS=${AS:-$BRANCH}
    34	[ "$AS" != "main" ] || { echo "push main through --promote on a branch, not as a branch name" >&2; exit 64; }
    35	
    36	say() { printf '\n▸ %s\n' "$*"; }
    37	ok()  { printf '  ✓ %s\n' "$*"; }

    39	
    40	# Subdomain Cloudflare derives from the branch name.

   126	[ $PROMOTE -eq 1 ] && echo "  Production: $PROD_URL ($SHORT)"
   127	echo "  Preview:    $PREVIEW_URL ($SHORT)"
   128	echo "  Now report to Akash: what changed, what is deployed (URL + commit), how to test it."

# Hosting spec: The Watchmaker's Bench

- **Production:** https://watchmakers-bench.pages.dev (branch `main`, verified 2026-11-03)
- **Previews:** every other branch deploys to `https://<branch>.watchmakers-bench.pages.dev` (verified 2026-11-03)
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/ahparikh/watchmakers-bench (public), Cloudflare Pages project `watchmakers-bench`

Goal: pushing to `main` on GitHub redeploys the static site to Cloudflare Pages within a couple
of minutes, with a preview URL for every other branch. No backend, no secrets, no runtime keys.

Decided 2026-11-01 (see CLAUDE.md "Decisions"): Cloudflare Pages over Vercel because the free
tier has no commercial-use clause and no bandwidth cap, and nothing in this project needs
Vercel's serverless features.

## What already exists

# The Watchmaker's Bench

A browser app where anyone learns why a mechanical watch runs fast or slow by diagnosing and regulating a live, simulated movement, read through a timegrapher (rate in s/day, amplitude in degrees, beat error in ms).

`watchmaker_brief.md` is the source of truth for concept and scope. `CLAUDE.md` carries decisions and working rules. `SPIKE.md` records the escapement spike that preceded this build.

## Development

Requires Node 22 or newer.

```sh
npm ci            # install (no browser downloads; Playwright browsers are fetched only by the verify-render skill)
npm run dev       # Vite dev server
npm run build     # tsc --noEmit, then vite build → dist/
npm run preview   # serve dist/ locally
npm test          # vitest run (sim core)
```

## Deployment

Static site on Cloudflare Pages. Pushing to `main` redeploys production; every other branch gets a preview URL. Agents deploy with the `deploy` skill (`.claude/skills/deploy/`): preview any branch any time, promote to `main` only on Akash's go-ahead. See `docs/hosting.md`, "Deploy process".

Production URL: https://watchmakers-bench.pages.dev

# Code review: The Watchmaker's Bench, 2026-11-16

Range `3522490..origin/main` (tip `2825770`, 37 commits, 50 files, about 3,900 lines): the whole application.
Review only; no application code was changed. Method: `mattpocock-skills:code-review` (Standards and Spec sub-agents in parallel, reports in the last section), plus a line-by-line read of `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` and the skill scripts, and numeric and headless-browser probes for every finding marked "measured".

## Verdict

1. The lumped physics (`src/core/oscillator`, `watch.ts`, `timegrapher/analyze.ts`) matches its research notes in form, sign and units; I found no wrong formula there.
2. The drawing contradicts that physics in two places a learner will see: the regulator moves the wrong way along the hairspring, and the heavy spot is drawn on the opposite side of the balance from where the model puts it.
3. Three behaviours are broken in the running app: "real time" speed runs at 7 fps, the two trace lines jump every frame in puzzle 2, and puzzle 4 solves in six seconds without diagnosing anything.
4. All five required checks pass, but they pass over these defects: the tests pin the wrong regulator direction, the screenshots carry a stray highlight, and `e2e-solve` cannot fail on two of its three puzzles.
5. Not ready to call the core "done" against its own rules; items 1 to 6 below are each a day or less and should land before any further stretch work.

## Evidence: the required checks

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | 8 files, 59 tests pass, 0 skipped. 10 of the 59 are `spike/tests/`, collected because there is no vitest config. |
| `npm run build` | `tsc --noEmit` clean; bundle 60.0 kB (21.4 kB gzip). |
| `verify-render.mjs --root .` | All 21 named states pass their numeric checks, no page errors. |
| `scripts/e2e-solve.mjs` | Exit 0; prints puzzles 1, 4, 3 solved (see finding 12 on what that is worth). |
| `scripts/drag-stability.mjs` | 24 of 24 slider drags hold still at 1280, 1000, 760 and 390 px. |
| `scripts/onboarding-e2e.mjs` (not asked for, run anyway) | All checks ok. |

## Findings, most severe first

Sizes: S under an hour, M half a day, L more than a day.

### 1. The regulator is drawn moving the wrong way, and its pins are not on the spring (M)

- **Where:** `src/core/escapement/adjustments.ts:93-96`, pinned by `tests/core/adjustments.test.ts:34-39` and `src/verify/states.ts:31`.
- **What:** positive index (toward F) moves the pins *toward* the stud. The code comment says this is "shortening the active coil".
- **Standard broken:** "Horology is verified before it becomes code". `docs/research/01-balance-period-and-regulator.md:38-39` says the opposite: "Moving the curb pins *away* from the stud shortens the active length (fast); toward the stud lengthens it (slow)." The model in `period.ts:28-30` is right; only the drawing is wrong.
- **Also (measured):** the pins sit 6.8 scene units from the nearest point of the hairspring polyline, with a half-gap of 2.2. They are placed 24° past the stud, where the outer coil has already ended, so they straddle nothing.
- **Failure scenario:** guide step 4 (`src/app/onboarding.ts:117-118`) says, correctly, that only the spring between the pins and the centre works and that F shortens it. The reader drags the slider toward F and watches the pins move toward the outer end, which lengthens that span.
- **Copy:** puzzle 1's explanation (`src/puzzles/index.ts:36`) says the pins "pinch the hairspring nearer its end, so a shorter length of spring does the work". Read with the guide's "outer end", that is backwards too.
- **Fix:** put the pins on the outer coil on the collet side of the stud, move them away from the stud for F, rewrite the test name and assertion, and reword the explanation.

### 2. The heavy spot is drawn 180° from where the physics puts it (S to M)

- **Where:** `src/core/watch.ts:15-18` (`down: 0` for crown up) against `src/core/escapement/adjustments.ts:54-62` (`CROWN_AT_DEG = 0`, crown up rotates +90°).
- **What:** the model treats rim angle 0° as pointing straight down in crown up. The drawing puts the crown at rim 0° and turns it to the top.
- **Measured:** with the watch stopped (balance at rest) and a poise cut at 0°, the cut is drawn above the balance centre in crown up, below it in crown down, and on the crown side in crown left and right. The physics has it on the opposite side in all four.
- **Failure scenario:** puzzle 4's hint (`onboarding.ts:36`) says "The heavy spot is at the bottom when crown up". The watch loses 6.1 s/day there, which is right for a bottom heavy spot at 250° (research 04). On solving, the revealed heavy spot appears at the top of the balance. Research 04 says a top heavy spot above 220° gains.
- **Why the tests miss it:** `watch.test.ts:48-56` checks only that crown up and crown down have opposite signs; nothing ties `POSITIONS.down` to the view rotation.
- **Fix:** derive both from one table (crown rim angle and which way is down per position) and add a test that the rim angle the model calls "down" is drawn pointing down the page.
- **Unsure:** which side should change. Changing `down` flips the puzzle's rate signs and the judgment-log entry of puzzle 4; changing the drawing's reference angle does not.

### 3. "Real time" speed cannot run (M)

- **Where:** `src/core/escapement/kinematics.ts:32,59-64,141-149`, driven from `src/main.ts:141-147`.
- **Measured:** one `step()` for a 16.7 ms frame at real time costs 24 ms in Node. In headless Chromium the page drops to 6.8 fps, and the movement advances 2.70 s in 4.00 wall seconds.
- **Cause:** 167 substeps per frame; while the wheel is locked, each substep runs `advance()`'s 40-iteration bisection, and every iteration rebuilds all 15 tooth polygons and both stones.
- **Knock-on:** `wallDt` is capped at 0.1 s (`main.ts:141`), so the timegrapher clock and the 60-second hold also run slow, and sliders lag. The default speed (1/10) costs 2.4 ms a frame and is fine.
- **Fix:** return early from `advance()` when the wheel is already against a face; test only the teeth near the stones; substep finely only while the pin is in the notch or the wheel is free. Add a budget test (one real-time frame under about 4 ms).

### 4. The trace's two lines jump by the beat error on almost every frame (S)

- **Where:** `src/core/timegrapher/analyze.ts:40`, fed by the sliding window in `src/app/ticker.ts:27`.
- **What:** each dot's offset is measured from `ticks[0]`. Once the window holds 300 ticks it slides by one tick at a time, so the anchor alternates between a tick and a tock.
- **Measured:** in puzzle 2 after nine seconds, the first parity-0 dot's `cy` alternated between 134.4 and 150 on 33 of 39 frames. The numeric probe shows the same thing: offsets flip between 0 and 2.73 ms.
- **Failure scenario:** puzzle 2 asks the user to watch two lines merge into one. After six wall seconds the lines swap places continuously.
- **Why the tests miss it:** `timegrapher.test.ts` analyses one fixed window; named states are frozen.
- **Fix:** anchor offsets to an absolute beat index and time carried in `TickWindow`, not to the first tick in the window. Add a test that sliding the window by one tick moves no dot.

### 5. Puzzle 4 completes on hidden state and needs no diagnosis (S)

- **Where:** `src/puzzles/index.ts:74-77`, `src/main.ts:197`.
- **What:** the band is `r.netUnbalance <= 1.5e-11`. It reads no instrument value and no position.
- **Spec line:** Decisions, "Solved when readouts stay in a target band". Brief: "Compare positions on the trace".
- **Measured:** load puzzle 4, move only the Poising amount to 10, leave Position on dial up: solved in 6.0 s. The fault is at 0° and the angle slider resets to 0, so the angle is never searched for.
- **Also:** the goal text promises "crown up and crown down each read within 3 s/day of dial up"; nothing checks it. (The numbers are consistent: at the band edge crown up reads +0.3 and crown down +2.6.)
- **Fix:** put the fault at a non-zero angle, and require the instrument rate to have been read in band in crown up and crown down (state the puzzle keeps), or drop the hold for a "compare and answer" ending like puzzle 3.

### 6. A first-time visitor lands in a nine-card modal and Free play, not puzzle 1 (S, needs Akash's call)

- **Where:** `src/app/onboarding.ts:445,516-517`.
- **Spec lines:** "A reviewer opens the link and is solving a puzzle within 30 seconds"; risk table, "Puzzle 1 opens by default with a one-line goal".
- **Measured:** with the guide enabled the job picker reads Free play and the card reads "Two minutes".
- **Test blind spot:** `navigator.webdriver` suppresses the guide, so `e2e-solve`, `drag-stability` and `verify-render` never see what a person sees.
- **Fix options:** open on puzzle 1 with the guide offered from the strip; or keep the guide but leave puzzle 1 loaded behind it. Replace the `webdriver` sniff with an explicit `?noguide` that the scripts pass.

### 7. Named-state screenshots are not what the state says (S)

- **Where:** `src/main.ts:197-201,223-245`.
- **What:** `loadPuzzle` dispatches `input` on every slider; each handler calls `touch(part)`, so the last one leaves `hot = "poise"` for 600 ms.
- **Measured:** `?state=runs-fast-start` (no highlight declared) has one `.part.hot` group and a dashed cut circle in the frozen drawing. The same flash shows on every live puzzle load.
- **Also:** `Object.assign(user, s.settings)` never updates the sliders. In `runs-fast-fixed` the regulator slider shows 0 and "+0.00°" while the state runs at −1.2°.
- **Also:** in `__bench.check`, `rateWithin`, `amplitudeWithin` and `beatErrorBelow` are skipped when `tg` is null (`main.ts:261-263`), and `pose.violations` is never checked.
- **Fix:** reset sliders without going through `touch`; set slider values from the state; fail a check whose input is missing.

### 8. `src/main.ts` is one 271-line module doing six jobs, none testable (M to L)

- **State and rules:** `effective()`, `loadPuzzle`, the hold timer (`:50-60,156-160,193-202`) are pure logic with no test. `heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? user.heavySpotDeg` and the additive faults are exactly the kind of line that needs one.
- **Rendering inside main:** `puzzleHtml()` (`:114-123`) builds the card, including hard-coded copy (`:121`, already in `docs/handoffs.md`).
- **Post-render patching:** `:97` overwrites the renderer's `.phase` text with "STOPPED · no torque at the escape wheel". That statement is false: measured, the healthy watch stops at 40 h with 26 % torque and the tired one at 38 h with 27 %. The stop is the model's 120° amplitude threshold.
- **Same conflation in the core:** `:147` passes `reading.running` as `step()`'s `driven` flag, documented in `kinematics.ts:56-57` as "a run-down watch has none".
- **Type holes:** `(user as any)[key]` (`:167`), `includes(name as never)` (`:125,129`); `|| puzzle.controls.length === 0` is dead.
- **Verify contract in the production bundle:** `:206-267`, including a 4,000-step scan.
- **Ownership:** CLAUDE.md gives onboarding one mount line and design none, so both reach in through the DOM instead (finding 13).
- **Fix:** `src/app/bench.ts` (state, `effective`, `loadPuzzle`, hold; pure, tested), `src/view/puzzleCard.ts`, `src/verify/contract.ts` behind `?state`, and `main.ts` as wiring only.

### 9. The tick stream that runs is not the one that is tested, and it invents ticks (S)

- **Where:** `src/app/ticker.ts:12-27` against `src/core/oscillator/ticks.ts:32-59`.
- **What:** `advanceTicks` re-implements `crossingDuration` and `tickTimes`. `tickTimes` is called only from tests; `advanceTicks` has none and lives in `src/app/`, though it is pure sim.
- **Measured:** run 10 s, stop for 100 sim-seconds, restart: the window fills with 299 ticks time-stamped inside the stopped interval. `nextTime` is not moved forward while stopped, so the restart back-fills.
- **Fix:** move it to `src/core/oscillator/`, build it on `beatIntervals` and an exported `crossingDuration`, set `nextTime = untilTime` while stopped, and test both.

### 10. Renderers compute (M)

- **Standard:** "Renderers read state and compute nothing"; `movement.ts:1` repeats the claim.
- **`src/view/movement.ts:41-51`:** frame size and viewBox chosen from the rotation.
- **`:60-70`:** spoke and wheel-arm angles from `balanceAngle` and `wheelAngle`, with literal `0.14 R`, `0.66 R`, `72`.
- **`:71-82`:** a nearest-tooth search to place the contact dot. It uses distance to the two corners, which is not the test `classify()` uses.
- **`:96-113`:** regulator arm start, track arcs, swing arcs.
- **`:99`:** `rg.scale.slow && 0 + (indexDeg - 10)` is an object `&&` a number; it works by accident.
- **Fix:** move these into `shapes()` and `adjustmentShapes()` as named outputs (contact point, spokes, arms, frame), and leave the view to format them.

### 11. Tests: what was restated, what is weak, what is missing

- **SPIKE's three restatements, my judgement:**
  - "Stationary while locked" excluding run to banking: a fair restatement. The lever does travel with the tooth on the locking face.
  - "Half a tooth per beat" lock-to-lock: fair, for the reason given (circular pallets).
  - "Never runs backward" with 0.001° allowed: no longer needed. Measured over seven trajectories (amplitude 122° to 280°, beat offset −10° to +10°, steps from 0.1 ms to 100 ms) the largest backward move was exactly 0 and `maxNudge` was 0. Tighten it to zero (S).
- **A fourth, unlisted:** the brief's "the pallet never overlaps a tooth" is tested as "no tooth *vertex* inside a stone" (`escapement.test.ts:105-110`). Measured: the exit let-off corner sits 0.044 units inside a tooth for 2 of 8,000 samples during drop. Invisible at wheel radius 100, but the test cannot see this class of overlap.
- **Tests of implementation:** `pin.test.ts:11` reads the notch by polygon index (`g.lever[7]`, `[6]`); `adjustments.test.ts:34` asserts a direction (finding 1).
- **Loose tolerances:** `toBeCloseTo(x, -1)` accepts ±5: "about +40 s/day" passes at 35.1 (`watch.test.ts:18,34,42`, `period.test.ts:31,35`).
- **Narrow coverage:** the escapement invariants run at one amplitude (270°), zero beat offset, and a private copy of the parameters (`escapement.test.ts:6-10`), not the catalog's. My probes at other amplitudes and offsets were clean; they should be tests.
- **No coverage:** `src/app/ticker.ts`, puzzle bands and hold, `effective()`, both views, `onboarding.ts` (Playwright only).
- **No vitest config:** `npm test` collects `spike/tests` here and other worktrees' copies in the shared checkout (open in `docs/handoffs.md` since 2026-11-03).

### 12. Scripts (S each)

- **`scripts/e2e-solve.mjs:15,21,25`:** prints `"puzzle 4 — solved:", true` as a literal; puzzles 1 and 3 print a boolean and exit 0 either way. Puzzle 2 is not exercised. Values are set by synthetic events, not a drag. A timeout leaves the server and browser open.
- **`verify-render.mjs:11,15`:** fixed port 5199 with `strictPort: true`; two agents running it at once collide. `ace91e8` fixed this only for the onboarding script. `:28` calls `process.exit(2)` before the `finally`.
- **`deploy.sh:72-73`:** runs the suite twice. The gate is tests and build only; CLAUDE.md asks for verify-render before "done" and the script does not run it.
- **Unsure:** `deploy.sh:41` does not truncate the preview subdomain. I believe Cloudflare shortens long branch aliases, which would make `wait_serve` time out on a long branch name; I did not verify the limit.

### 13. Onboarding and the speed control talk to main through the DOM (M)

- **Ids `onboarding.ts` depends on:** `puzzle-select`, `puzzle`, `speed-slider`, `regulator`, `beat`, `wind`, `screws`, `poise`, `poise-angle`, `position`, `ctl-*`, `timegrapher`, and SVG classes `balance`, `mark`, `centreline`, `gravity`.
- **Silent failure:** every lookup is optional-chained (`:254,365,372,385`), so a renamed id does nothing and throws nothing.
- **Text parsing:** `progressed()` (`:490-495`) reads the hold bar's text and tests `startsWith("0 /")`.
- **Synthetic events as an API:** `pointerdown`/`pointerup` to hold a highlight (`:382-388`), `input` and `change` to reset controls and pick a puzzle.
- **`src/view/speed.ts:26-27`:** drives a hidden `<select>` with a synthetic `change`; `index.html:252-257` mounts it from an inline module and re-parents `#onboarding`. It is a controller filed under `view/`.
- **Fix:** a small typed object exported by the app (`selectPuzzle`, `setSpeed`, `highlight`, `resetControls`, `onProgress`), which the 2026-11-13 handoff already asks for.

### 14. The catalog does not feed the app (S to M)

- `src/catalog/vintage18000.ts:10-25` states the beat rate three times, the lift angle three times, and inertia, length and radius twice.
- `Calibre.inertia`, `activeLength`, `regulatorRadius`, `amplitude` and `puzzles` are never read; `afterDayDeg: 250` can drift from the model.
- Slider ranges are literals in `index.html:238-243` (wind `max="42"`); `main.ts:192` lists every puzzle regardless of `calibre.puzzles`.
- Spec line: "A watch catalog … feeds the controls, so a new watch is data, not code."

### 15. Smaller physics and copy points

- **`watch.ts:94`:** knocking adds an unnamed `120` s/day. Research 03 gives "+50 to +300", low confidence. It is also unreachable: amplitude never exceeds 280°.
- **Puzzle 3 is faint:** +1.9 s/day at 12 h and +3.3 at 24 h, shown as whole seconds, and inside the ±5 band puzzle 1 calls fixed. The goal says slide to 40 h; this watch stops at 38 h.
- **Puzzle 4 symptom:** "loses on the wrist", but only crown up loses (−6.1); crown down gains 9.0; crown left and right gain 1.4.
- **Unsure:** the trace slopes down for a gaining watch. I believe Witschi and Weishi screens slope up for a gain; research 02 verified only `tg`'s vertical strip. Worth one `/research` pass, since the strip's explainer teaches the direction.
- **`classify()` (`kinematics.ts:116`):** the lock-arc distance ignores the arc's angular extent, so any tooth tip at the lock radius counts. No misfire observed.

### 16. Stale docs, dead code, leftover branches (S)

- **CLAUDE.md:** "Stack (planned)"; "Next: stretch items … each on its own branch" while puzzles 2 to 4 are on `main`; the Harness Lab brief note.
- **`docs/hosting.md` "What already exists":** still describes an untracked folder with a placeholder page and tells agents not to edit `src/`.
- **`docs/handoffs.md`:** lines 7 and 8 are superseded by line 12; three requests are open (vitest exclude, `whyWrong`, highlight hook).
- **Stale comments:** `GLOSSARY.md:3-4`, `catalog/types.ts:18`, `escapement.test.ts:6`; `kinematics.ts:2` says "Swiss lever" (a comment, not UI copy).
- **Glossary gaps:** `unbalance`, `knocking`, `collet`, balance cock, `tilt`.
- **Dead code:** `geom2d.penetration`, `Reading.beats`, `WatchReading.torqueFraction`, `AdjustmentShapes.scale.centre`, `docs/deploy-check.txt`.
- **Branches:** `origin/adjustment-visuals` (its one commit is on `main` as `1c379aa`); `origin/worktree-brag-video` (one unmerged commit, `b0966a5`); local `design-doc` (two unmerged); `worktree-onboarding` (merged).

## What is solid

- **The physics core.** `period.ts`, `amplitude.ts`, `poise.ts`, `bessel.ts`, `ticks.ts` and `analyze.ts` are pure, small, and each formula matches its research note: T = 2π√(I/k) with k ∝ 1/L; rate = 86400(T₀/T − 1); beat error |d2 − d1|/2 (2.73 ms for 6° at 280°, as logged); the sine form of the amplitude formula; the J1 poise term with the right crossover.
- **The two-layer rule holds.** No rate, amplitude or beat error is read from the drawing; the instrument and the model agree to 0.01 s/day in every named state.
- **The contact solver is robust.** Across amplitudes 122° to 280°, beat offsets of ±10° and caller steps up to 100 ms: exactly 96° of wheel travel in four periods, zero violations, zero backward motion. `step()` is pure; the only history is the previous pose.
- **No tests skipped, deleted or loosened in the range.**
- **Process artefacts work.** `docs/judgment-log.md` is honest and specific; `drag-stability.mjs` is a good regression test for a real bug; `deploy.sh` refuses rewrites and non-fast-forward promotes.
- **Mobile meets its bar.** At 390 px there is no horizontal scroll and puzzle 1 solves with a real pointer drag (measured).
- **Decisions honoured:** 18,000 bph, fixed 52° label, picker hidden, 10× instrument clock, two-choice ending for puzzle 3, no "Swiss lever" in UI copy.

## Standards and Spec reports (from the skill's two sub-agents, lightly cleaned)

The two axes are kept separate on purpose and are not merged with the ranking above.

<tr><th width="50%">Standards</th><th width="50%">Spec</th></tr>
<tr><td valign="top">

**Documented-standard breaches**

1. **Renderer computes** (CLAUDE.md "Simulation and rendering never mix").
   - `src/view/movement.ts:60-70`: spoke and arm angles, literals `0.14*R`, `0.66*R`, `72`.
   - `:71-82`: nearest-tooth search for the contact dot.
   - `:96`, `:99`, `:110-113`: regulator arm start, track arcs, swing arcs.
   - `:99`: `rg.scale.slow && 0 + (indexDeg - 10)` works by accident.
   - `src/main.ts:97`: overwrites the renderer's `.phase` text.
2. **Geometry outside the one config object** ("Geometry is derived, never drawn").

Akash, the review is written and committed as 79a04e3 on branch code-review (not pushed, nothing deployed, no application code changed).

Verdict

  1. The lumped physics (src/core/oscillator, watch.ts, analyze.ts) matches its research notes in form, sign and units; I found no wrong formula there.
  2. The drawing contradicts that physics in two places a learner will see: the regulator moves the wrong way along the hairspring, and the heavy spot is drawn on the opposite side of the balance from where the model puts it.
  3. Three behaviours are broken in the running app: "real time" speed runs at about 7 fps, the two trace lines jump every frame in puzzle 2, and puzzle 4 solves in six seconds without any diagnosis.
  4. All five required checks pass, but they pass over these defects: a test pins the wrong regulator direction, the screenshots carry a stray highlight, and e2e-solve cannot fail on two of its three puzzles.
  5. The core is not "done" against its own rules; findings 1 to 6 in the report are each a day or less and should land before more stretch work.

Top five findings

  1. Regulator drawn backwards (src/core/escapement/adjustments.ts:93-96). Toward F moves the pins toward the stud, which lengthens the working spring. Research 01 and the guide's own step 4 say the opposite, and tests/core/adjustments.test.ts:34 asserts the wrong direction. The pins also sit 6.8 units off the spring, so they straddle nothing.
  2. Heavy spot drawn 180° from the physics (src/core/watch.ts:15-18 against adjustments.ts:54-62). The model treats rim 0° as the bottom in crown up, while the drawing puts it at the top. Puzzle 4's hint says "at the bottom", the watch loses as a bottom heavy spot should, then the reveal shows it at the top. I'm unsure which side should change.
  3. "Real time" speed cannot run (src/core/escapement/kinematics.ts:59-64,141-149). One 16.7 ms frame costs 24 ms of solver time. In headless Chromium that gave 6.8 fps and 2.7 s of movement per 4 wall seconds, and it slows the timegrapher clock and hold timer too. The default 1/10 speed is fine.
  4. Trace lines jump in puzzle 2 (src/core/timegrapher/analyze.ts:40). Offsets are anchored to the first tick in a sliding window, so once the window fills the two lines swap by the beat error. The first dot moved on 33 of 39 frames.
  5. Puzzle 4 completes on hidden state (src/puzzles/index.ts:74-77). The band reads netUnbalance, not the instrument. It solved in 6.0 s in dial up by moving only the amount slider, because the fault is at 0° and the angle slider resets to 0.

Next in the ranking is a spec call for you: a first-time visitor lands in a nine-card guide and Free play rather than puzzle 1, and the scripts never see this because navigator.webdriver suppresses the guide.

Check results

npm run build clean, 60 kB bundle
verify-render all 21 named states pass
e2e-solve exit 0

Other unsure points are listed at the end of the report: Cloudflare's branch-alias length limit, and which way a real timegrapher's trace slopes for a gaining watch.

Assistant2026-11-17T06:46:39.739Z

Fix six things, in this order, and leave the rest.

  1. Regulator direction (finding 1). This is the one place the app teaches something false, and puzzle 1 is the first thing anyone touches. Move the pins onto the outer coil, make F move them away from the stud, flip the test, and reword the puzzle 1 explanation. Half a day.
  2. Heavy spot side (finding 2). Change the drawing's reference angle, not POSITIONS.down. That keeps the rate signs, the puzzle 4 states and the judgment-log entry as they are, and makes the reveal agree with the hint. Add one test tying "down" in the model to down on the page. About an hour.
  3. Trace jitter (finding 4). Anchor dot offsets to an absolute beat index instead of the first tick in the window. Under an hour, and puzzle 2 is unreadable without it.
  4. Puzzle 4 completion (finding 5). Put the fault at a non-zero angle and require the rate to have been read in crown up and crown down before the hold counts. Under an hour, and it restores the diagnosis the puzzle exists for.
  5. Real-time speed (finding 3). The cheap fix is an early return in advance() when the wheel is already against a face, which removes most of the cost while locked. If that does not get a frame under about 4 ms, drop the "real time" stop rather than spend more of the 8 hours on it; the brief only asks for real time down to slow motion, and 1/5 already runs well.
  6. First visit (finding 6). I would leave puzzle 1 loaded and offer the guide from the strip, because the brief's "solving a puzzle within 30 seconds" is the reviewer's first impression. This one is your call, since it undoes a deliberate onboarding choice.

Two small ones are worth doing alongside because they stop the checks from hiding the above:

  • e2e-solve: make it assert and exit non-zero, and replace the navigator.webdriver sniff with an explicit ?noguide.
  • Screenshots: stop loadPuzzle from leaving the poise highlight on, so the verify-render shots show what the state says.

I would not fix these now:

  • The main.ts split, renderers computing, the catalog, DOM coupling (findings 8, 10, 13, 14). They are real, but they are structure, not behaviour, and each is half a day or more. Name them in the design doc as known debt.
  • The "no torque" label (in finding 8). Worth a one-line copy change to "STOPPED" if you are in that file anyway.
  • Stale docs and branches (finding 16). Ten minutes of tidying at the end, not before.

One thing to check before you start: whether a real timegrapher's trace slopes up or down for a gaining watch. I was unsure, and the strip's explainer teaches the direction, so if it is wrong it belongs with item 1.

The search didn't directly answer the question. None of the results say which way a rising trace on a Witschi timegrapher means gain or loss.

- **Witschi X1 manual:** The Chronoscope X1 (G3) manual has a trace display mode, but the snippet cuts off at The slope of the diagram can be, so the direction isn't stated.
- **General timegrapher guide:** A Time and Tide article says the readouts are "rate", "amplitude", "beat error", and "parameters" (also referred to as the beat rate). It doesn't cover trace slope in the snippet.
- **Racelogic (unrelated context):** A lap-timing tool states that when the Delta-T is increasing, you are losing time, when it is decreasing, you are gaining time. That's a different instrument and measure, so it doesn't settle the timegrapher question.

From general knowledge rather than these results: on most timegraphers, the trace is a plot of time error over time, so a steady upward or downward drift means a consistent rate error. Whether up means fast or slow depends on the device's axis convention. Check the Witschi Weishi manual's trace or diagram section, or compare against a watch with a known rate error, to confirm the sign.

/** Completion rule for a puzzle, as a pure step: has the band been held long enough, and (for a
 *  puzzle that must be checked in several positions) in every one of them? No DOM, no clock. */
import type { Puzzle } from "./index";
import type { Position, WatchReading } from "../core/watch";
import type { Reading } from "../core/timegrapher/analyze";

export interface Progress {
  /** Sim seconds the band has been held without a break (in the current position, if positions matter). */
  heldSeconds: number;
  /** Positions in which the hold has been completed since the band last failed. */
  passed: Position[];
  solved: boolean;
}

export const NO_PROGRESS: Progress = { heldSeconds: 0, passed: [], solved: false };

/** Advance by `dt` sim seconds with the watch as it reads now, in `position`. */
export function advanceProgress(puzzle: Puzzle, was: Progress, r: WatchReading, tg: Reading | null, position: Position, dt: number): Progress {
  if (was.solved || !Number.isFinite(puzzle.holdSeconds)) return was;
  // Out of band anywhere: start again. A position passed before a failure proves nothing about the watch as it is now.
  if (!puzzle.band(r, tg)) return NO_PROGRESS;
  if (!puzzle.holdIn) {
    const heldSeconds = was.heldSeconds + dt;
    return { heldSeconds, passed: [], solved: heldSeconds >= puzzle.holdSeconds };
  }
  // In band, but this position is not one that counts, or it has been passed already: wait for the next one.
  if (!puzzle.holdIn.includes(position) || was.passed.includes(position)) return { ...was, heldSeconds: 0 };
  const heldSeconds = was.heldSeconds + dt;
  if (heldSeconds < puzzle.holdSeconds) return { ...was, heldSeconds };
  const passed = [...was.passed, position];
  return { heldSeconds: 0, passed, solved: puzzle.holdIn.every((p) => passed.includes(p)) };
}
EOF

import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import { PUZZLES } from "../../src/puzzles";
import { advanceProgress, NO_PROGRESS, type Progress } from "../../src/puzzles/progress";
import { readWatch, ZERO_SETTINGS, type Position, type WatchSettings } from "../../src/core/watch";
import { VINTAGE_18000 } from "../../src/catalog/vintage18000";
import { advanceTicks, emptyWindow } from "../../src/app/ticker";
import { analyze } from "../../src/core/timegrapher/analyze";

const puzzle = (id: string) => PUZZLES.find((p) => p.id === id)!;
const T = 0.4;

/** Hold the watch at `user` settings (puzzle faults added, as the app does) for `seconds` of sim time. */
function hold(id: string, user: Partial<WatchSettings>, seconds: number, from: Progress = NO_PROGRESS): Progress {
  const p = puzzle(id), f = p.faults;
  const s: WatchSettings = { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, ...user,
    regulatorIndex: (user.regulatorIndex ?? 0) + (f.regulatorIndex ?? 0), beatOffsetDeg: (user.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0) + (f.beatOffsetDeg ?? 0),
    unbalance: f.unbalance ?? 0, heavySpotDeg: f.heavySpotDeg ?? 0 };
  const r = readWatch(p.specOverride ? p.specOverride(VINTAGE_18000.watch) : VINTAGE_18000.watch, s);
  const tg = analyze(advanceTicks(emptyWindow(), r, 60, 300).ticks, T, 52);
  let prog = from;
  for (let t = 0; t < seconds; t += 0.5) prog = advanceProgress(p, prog, r, tg, s.position, 0.5);
  return prog;
}

describe("puzzle 1 completion", () => {
  it("is not solved as loaded, and is solved after 60 s with the regulator moved 1.2° toward Slow", () => {
    expect(hold("runs-fast", {}, 120).solved).toBe(false);
    expect(hold("runs-fast", { regulatorIndex: -1.2 }, 59).solved).toBe(false);
    expect(hold("runs-fast", { regulatorIndex: -1.2 }, 60).solved).toBe(true);
  });
  it("starts the hold again when the reading leaves the band", () => {
    const part = hold("runs-fast", { regulatorIndex: -1.2 }, 40);
    expect(hold("runs-fast", {}, 1, part).heldSeconds).toBe(0);
  });
});

describe("puzzle 4 completion", () => {
  const fix = { poiseCorrection: 10e-11, poiseCorrectionDeg: 180 };
  const round = (user: Partial<WatchSettings>, positions: Position[], from: Progress = NO_PROGRESS) =>
    positions.reduce((prog, position) => hold("position-error", { ...user, position }, 15, prog), from);

  it("shows the fault in the instrument: crown down loses, crown up gains, the other two barely move", () => {
    const rate = (position: Position) => readWatch(VINTAGE_18000.watch, { ...ZERO_SETTINGS, ...puzzle("position-error").faults, position }).rateSecondsPerDay;
    expect(rate("CD")).toBeLessThan(-3);
    expect(rate("CU")).toBeGreaterThan(3);
    expect(Math.abs(rate("CR"))).toBeLessThan(3);
    expect(Math.abs(rate("CL"))).toBeLessThan(3);
    expect(Math.abs(rate("DU"))).toBeLessThan(0.01);
  });
  it("is not solved by removing weight without ever leaving dial up", () => {
    expect(hold("position-error", fix, 600).solved).toBe(false);
  });
  it("is not solved by removing the right amount at the control's resting angle", () => {
    expect(round({ poiseCorrection: 10e-11, poiseCorrectionDeg: 0 }, ["CU", "CR", "CD", "CL"]).solved).toBe(false);
  });
  it("is not solved by running the watch down to the 220° crossover, where the error hides", () => {
    for (const hoursSinceWind of [20, 22, 24, 26]) expect(round({ hoursSinceWind }, ["CU", "CR", "CD", "CL"]).solved).toBe(false);
  });
  it("is solved once the rate has been shown in band in all four crown positions, in any order", () => {
    const three = round(fix, ["CD", "CU", "CL"]);
    expect(three.solved).toBe(false);
    expect(three.passed).toEqual(["CD", "CU", "CL"]);
    expect(round(fix, ["CR"], three).solved).toBe(true);
  });
  it("forgets positions passed before the watch went out of band", () => {
    // Crown right and left read in band even unrepaired; crown down then fails and clears them.
    const early = round({}, ["CR", "CL"]);
    expect(early.passed).toEqual(["CR", "CL"]);
    expect(round({}, ["CD"], early).passed).toEqual([]);
  });
});

// Can each puzzle be solved through the page, and does the page refuse the shortcuts?
// Exits non-zero if any check fails. Loads "/" exactly as a visitor does (no special URL).
import { chromium } from "playwright";
import { createServer } from "vite";
const server = await createServer({ root: process.cwd(), server: { port: 5198, strictPort: false }, logLevel: "silent" });
await server.listen();
const base = server.resolvedUrls.local[0];
const browser = await chromium.launch();
const out = [];
const check = (name, ok, detail = "") => out.push(`${ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL"} ${name} ${detail}`);
try {
  const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 900, height: 900 } });
  const errs = []; page.on("pageerror", (e) => errs.push(String(e)));
  const card = () => page.textContent("#puzzle");
  const solved = async (ms) => { try { await page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelector("#puzzle")?.textContent?.includes("Why it worked"), null, { timeout: ms }); return true; } catch { return false; } };
  const set = (id, v) => page.evaluate(([id, v]) => { const el = document.querySelector("#" + id); el.value = v; el.dispatchEvent(new Event("input")); }, [id, v]);

  await page.goto(base);
  await page.waitForSelector("#puzzle h2");
  check("a visitor lands on puzzle 1, no dialog in the way", (await card()).includes("Runs fast") && !(await page.isVisible("#guide")));
  check("the guide is offered in the strip", await page.isVisible('[data-act="replay"]'));
  check("nothing on the drawing is lit on load", (await page.$$("#movement .part.hot")).length === 0);

  // Puzzle 1: not solved as loaded; solved with the regulator at −1.2°.
  await page.waitForTimeout(3000);
  check("puzzle 1 is not solved as loaded", !(await card()).includes("Why it worked") && (await card()).includes("0 / 60 s in band"));
  await set("regulator", "-1.2");
  check("puzzle 1 solves with the regulator 1.2° toward S", await solved(40000));

  // Puzzle 2: solved by taking out the 6° beat offset.
  await page.selectOption("#puzzle-select", "out-of-beat");
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  check("puzzle 2 is not solved as loaded", !(await card()).includes("Why it worked"));
  await set("beat", "-6");
  check("puzzle 2 solves with the beat adjustment at −6°", await solved(40000));

  // Puzzle 3: the wrong answer does not solve it, the right one does.
  await page.selectOption("#puzzle-select", "afternoon-slump");
  await page.click('.choice[data-choice="0"]');
  check("puzzle 3 wrong answer is not accepted", !(await card()).includes("Why it worked"));
  await page.click('.choice[data-choice="1"]');
  check("puzzle 3 right answer is accepted", (await card()).includes("Why it worked"));

  // Puzzle 4: removing weight without diagnosing must not solve it; the full procedure must.
  await page.selectOption("#puzzle-select", "position-error");
  await set("poise", "10");
  await page.waitForTimeout(9000);
  check("puzzle 4 is not solved by the amount slider alone in dial up", !(await card()).includes("Why it worked"));
  for (const pos of ["CU", "CR", "CD", "CL"]) { await page.selectOption("#position", pos); await page.waitForTimeout(3500); }
  check("puzzle 4 is not solved by touring the positions with the weight removed at the wrong place", !(await card()).includes("Why it worked"));
  await set("poise-angle", "180");
  for (const pos of ["CU", "CR", "CD", "CL"]) {
    await page.selectOption("#position", pos);
    const mark = `✓ ${await page.$eval(`#position option[value="${pos}"]`, (o) => o.textContent)}`;
    let ok = true;
    try { await page.waitForFunction((m) => document.querySelector("#puzzle")?.textContent?.includes(m) || document.querySelector("#puzzle")?.textContent?.includes("Why it worked"), mark, { timeout: 20000 }); } catch { ok = false; }
    check(`puzzle 4 passes ${pos} once the rate is in band there`, ok);
  }
  check("puzzle 4 solves after all four crown positions", await solved(5000));
  check("no page errors", errs.length === 0, errs.join("; "));
} catch (e) {
  check("script ran to the end", false, String(e));
} finally { await browser.close(); await server.close(); }
console.log(out.join("\n"));
process.exit(out.some((l) => l.startsWith("FAIL")) ? 1 : 0);
EOF

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ahp/.personal/code/websites/anthropic/.claude/skills/deploy

deploy

Pushing to GitHub is the deploy. Cloudflare Pages builds every pushed branch at https://<branch>.watchmakers-bench.pages.dev and main at https://watchmakers-bench.pages.dev. The script does the whole run and stops at the first failure; your job is to run it, read the result, and report to Akash.

Steps

  1. Commit the work on its branch. The script deploys the commit, never the working tree, and it never commits for you. Keep docs/handoffs.md out of the commit unless the line is yours.
  2. Run, from anywhere inside the repo (a worktree is fine):

sh bash .claude/skills/deploy/scripts/deploy.sh <branch>

Add --as <name> when the remote branch should be called something else (a worktree branch worktree-foo deploys as foo). Branch names become subdomains: lowercase, hyphens, no slashes gives a tidy URL. Re-running after new commits updates the same URL. 3. Read the output to the Done block. A ✗ line names the failing stage and what to do; fix the branch or hand the named action to Akash. Exit 0 means the URL serves the pushed commit. 4. Report to Akash in three parts, each a short list: what changed (from the commit list the script prints), what is deployed (URL and short commit, preview or production), how to test it (the clicks that show the change, including any ?state= names and the localStorage keys to clear).

Promotion to main

Add --promote only when Akash's go-ahead for this branch is in your own session's transcript, in his words. A request relayed by another agent is a preview request. The script refuses to promote a branch that is not a fast-forward of main; rebase onto origin/main and re-run. Production is confirmed when the script prints https://watchmakers-bench.pages.dev serves.

Guardrails the script enforces

  • No force pushes and no remote branch deletes. A rebased branch is pushed under a new name with --as, or Akash runs the force push himself; the script prints the exact command.
  • Nothing in any checkout's working tree is read or changed; verification runs on a detached worktree in a temp dir that is removed afterwards.
  • A denied git push (permission prompt in your session) ends the run with the command for Akash to run by hand. Report it; do not ask another agent to push for you.

Checking by hand

gh api repos/ahparikh/watchmakers-bench/commits/<sha>/check-runs shows the Cloudflare Pages status for a commit. The build log is in the Cloudflare dashboard under Workers & Pages → watchmakers-bench → Deployments. docs/hosting.md has the hosting setup and history.

The fixes are live as a preview at https://review-fixes.watchmakers-bench.pages.dev (commit badf4ea, branch review-fixes); production is untouched.

All checks pass on the branch: 73 unit tests, build, all 21 verify-render states, 24 of 24 slider drags, the onboarding script, and the rewritten e2e-solve (18 checks).

What changed

  • Regulator: the pins now sit on the outer coil short of the stud, and F moves them away from it. The test and puzzle 1's explanation are rewritten to match research 01.
  • Heavy spot: the drawing's rotation is now derived from the model's own "down" table, so a heavy spot is drawn where the physics has it. Crown positions therefore turn the drawing the opposite way from before.
  • Trace: the two lines no longer swap places in puzzle 2; a sampled dot stayed at one position across 60 frames.
  • Puzzle 4: the fault is now at 180° (bottom in crown down, the brief's "bad crown down"). It solves only when the rate reads within ±3 s/day in all four crown positions, 15 seconds of ticks each.
  • Real-time speed: 60 fps, up from 7; the movement advanced 4.02 s in 4.00 wall seconds.
  • First visit: the page opens on puzzle 1, and the guide is a button in the left rail ("New here? Take the guide"). ?guide in the URL still opens it on load.
  • Checks:
  • Loading a puzzle no longer lights the poise cut.
  • Named states set their sliders.
  • e2e-solve now asserts, covers all four puzzles plus the shortcuts that must fail, and exits non-zero on failure.
  • Stopped label: now reads "STOPPED · the mainspring has run down" in place of the "no torque" claim.

How to test

  1. First visit: open the link in a private window. You should land on puzzle 1 with no dialog.
  2. Regulator: in puzzle 1, drag Regulator index toward F and watch the pointer move away from the stud, along the spring.
  3. Trace: switch to puzzle 2 and wait ten seconds. The two lines should hold still.
  4. Puzzle 4, shortcut: move only the Poising amount to 10 and stay in dial up. It should not solve.
  5. Puzzle 4, proper solve: set the angle to 180°, then visit crown up, right, down and left. Each gets a tick under the bar and the heavy spot is revealed at the bottom in crown down.
  6. Speed: drag Movement speed to "real time". It should run smoothly.

Things to know

  • Puzzle 4 still checks the hidden unbalance alongside the instrument reading. Without it, running the watch down to about 24 h (the 220° crossover) hides the poise error and would count as a repair.
  • The real-time guard is a browser check, not a unit test. A timing unit test was flaky under load, so the 30 fps floor lives in e2e-solve.
  • The trace slope direction is unchanged. One search did not settle which way a real timegrapher slopes for a gaining watch, so it still needs a /research pass.
  • main has moved since I branched. The deploy script reports the branch is not a fast-forward of origin/main, so it needs a rebase before any promote.
  • I edited files across all four owners. There is a line in docs/handoffs.md saying so, and four rows in docs/judgment-log.md recording the corrections.
